items.title: envelfo
items.text:
Reusable envelopes, LFOs, and event-driven control signals

The API Reference is generated from the Python source code.

items.title: Extraction closeout audit
items.text: Audit date: 2026-10-15. This records implementation ownership and verification, not an allocation-free audio callback guarantee or a promise of additional APIs.

The core's shared fixtures are envelfo-runtime.json, envelfo-patch.json, envelfo-host.json and envelfo-streams.json. Expected timestamps, pending deliveries, event order and random words are exact. Floating signals have absolute tolerance 1e-12. Host expectations are handwritten from elapsed-time, waveform and ordering rules, not generated from either implementation. The fixture Rust host is test-only; the core does not acquire or estimate tempo. Legacy invalid-document fixtures now use the canonical score discriminator and assert a body validation error, rather than passing because an obsolete score kind was rejected before its generator was checked.

items.title: Ownership and duplicate-path review
items.text:
• uFor contains authored definitions, validation, portable state records, stream identities, and stateless mathematics. It does not import enveLFO.
  • The older ufor.lfo definition/state/event/value classes and executable initializer/query/command functions have been removed, without aliases. Lighting uses ufor.envelfo.LFO with shape, resolved rates, seconds, part scope and free reset. Its stateless score calculations share waveform and activation mathematics; they do not maintain a second playback state.
  • enge block sampling accepts canonical LFO and EnvelfoState, without translating through a second LFO model or runtime. NumPy interpolation, vectorized spans, waveform kernels and sample-frame mapping remain audio acceleration, not alternate command/event schedulers.
  • Native named Envelopes, LFOs, Stages and retained Patch scheduling use envelfo-core. Python Patch scheduling uses envelfo.patch. Audio hosts retain scope admission, trigger addresses, minimum hold and retirement.
  • arpeg retains note/rhythm decisions and captured controller ownership. Its bridge links the libraries without making either event core depend on the other.

items.title: Deliberate limits, not missing extraction
items.text:
• Rust time has checked signed 64-bit rational components, i128 intermediates and explicit overflow errors. Python Fractions are not limited to that range.
  • Rust accepts normalized definitions and host clock mappings, not Pint strings, authored document parsing or MIDI clock acquisition.
  • Python snapshots serialize to JSON. Rust's optional snapshots feature bundles normalized definitions and complete state in versioned JSON, including Patch pending connections and RNG streams. Cross-language interchange is not provided. Hosts save clock mappings and external delivery queues themselves; combined enge/arpeg application snapshots remain host-owned.
  • Stateful operators require the same observation schedule for equivalent continuation. Additional observations can legitimately change their output.
  • Scalar LFO onset is a separate activation weight; staged LFO onset scales depth while preserving center. These existing contracts remain distinct.
  • enge's linear-only preparation restrictions, voice-amplitude profile policy and event-free audio accelerators are host restrictions, not absent core curves.
  • Standalone Python bindings to Rust remain optional and are not implemented.
  • arpeg's Python and Rust players now separate scheduling from MIDI realization. Hosts deliver all same-time hits, observe once, and realize fresh expression before note-on. Note-offs retain their ordering; no same-time feedback loop or automatic observation cadence is introduced. Shared wire traces cover the composition and captured/current expression ownership.

items.title: Distribution and licenses
items.text:
Python's runtime dependency is uFor, bringing Pydantic, reccy's Pint utilities and their declared dependencies. Neither NumPy nor enge is required. The wheel and source distribution build independently of enge and native bindings. Dependency revisions come from uv.lock for reproducible repository installs; publishing packages still requires their dependencies to be available.

The Rust runtime tree contains num-rational/num-integer/num-traits and RustCrypto SHA-256 dependencies, without num-rational's default BigInt feature. It contains no Python, PyO3, MIDI device host or audio engine. The crate packages and verifies independently. Its packaged LICENSE carries the project's MIT notices. The root and crate copies of that notice must stay identical. Enabling snapshots adds optional Serde/serde_json dependencies; the default runtime dependency tree is unchanged. JSON parsing enables exact float round trips.

The reviewed runtime manifests identify enveLFO, uFor and reccy as MIT; Rust runtime dependencies are MIT or dual MIT/Apache-2.0. Retain dependency notices when redistributing. This inventory is not a legal opinion or a statement that an application's unrelated optional audio dependencies share these licenses.

items.title: Verification and release boundary
items.text:
Local audit verification covers Python 3.13 and 3.15 on macOS, Rust debug/release tests and strict lint, wheel/source-distribution builds, Cargo package verification, and an installed-wheel test run outside the checkout with no NumPy or enge. Consumer verification covers uFor, enge and arpeg. These automated tests do not claim hardware, allocation-free callback, or physical MIDI timing validation.

Reproduce the source checks with:

uv sync --frozen
uv run --no-sync pytest
uv run --no-sync ruff check --select B,E,F,I envelfo test
uv run --no-sync ruff format --check envelfo test
uv run --no-sync ty check envelfo
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --workspace --locked --release
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked --features snapshots
cargo test --workspace --locked --release --features snapshots
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --features snapshots -- -D warnings
uv build
cargo package --manifest-path crates/envelfo-core/Cargo.toml --locked
cargo package --manifest-path crates/envelfo-core/Cargo.toml --locked --features snapshots

.github/workflows/test.yml runs only when a release is published. It gates Linux, Windows and macOS, Python 3.13/3.15, tests against a wheel installed in a fresh environment outside the checkout, and standalone Rust package verification. Rust checks run with snapshots disabled and enabled, including debug/release tests and independent package compilation. The enabled shared conformance runner serializes and reloads every continuation step, not just explicit restore points. The full repository tests retain access to the shared fixtures; the published crate's build verification is independent of those repository-level test assets. Cross-platform results are not claimed until that release workflow runs. This audit does not create a tag, publish packages or trigger a release.

items.title: MIDI output from named observations
items.text:
The optional Python envelfo.midi module and Rust envelfo-midi crate map already observed named values to meedee MIDI 1.0 messages. They do not acquire time, advance a Patch, send MIDI, own connections, or start threads. Observation times and delivery remain host responsibilities. Core enveLFO imports and the default Rust workspace member remain free of meedee and native MIDI build requirements.

Install Python support with uv sync --extra midi. The optional Rust crate uses meedee from HTTPS/main, requiring Rust 1.87, CMake and a C++20 compiler. Linux source builds additionally require ALSA headers and pkg-config. For example, Debian/Ubuntu uses libasound2-dev and pkg-config. The standalone core retains Rust 1.85. No CLI or audio-device host is added.

items.title: Mapping contract
items.text:
Python mappings are frozen Pydantic models; Rust mappings are checked immutable values. Each mapping names one output, an explicit increasing finite input range, a MIDI target and optional integer destination bounds. Multiple targets can read the same output. All mapped outputs must be present in each observation; other outputs are ignored. Mappings execute in declaration order. Duplicate logical destinations are rejected, including duplicate parameter IDs with different resolutions. The host must also avoid conflicting writes through other mappings, clients or applications; CC and fine-CC targets can overlap on the wire.

Python target Rust target MIDI value range CCTarget Target::ControlChange 0–127 FineCCTarget Target::ControlChange14 0–16383 RpnTarget Target::Rpn 0–127 or 0–16383, explicit resolution 7 or 14 NrpnTarget Target::Nrpn 0–127 or 0–16383, explicit resolution 7 or 14

Channels are 1–16. Ordinary controller IDs are 0–127; fine-CC base controllers are 0–31. RPN parameter 16383 is reserved for null selection; NRPN 16383 remains usable. RPN/NRPN Set commands select afresh and release with RPN null, using meedee's existing ordered expansion. No interpretation of vendor NRPN meanings is attempted. UMP and increment/decrement targets are outside this slice.

Destination minimum defaults to zero; maximum=None uses the target's full range. Explicit bounds must satisfy 0 <= minimum <= maximum <= native maximum. A constant destination range is allowed. Input ranges must have a positive finite width. Values outside those ranges, non-finite numbers and missing mapped outputs fail before admitting any batch. No clamping occurs. Python also rejects boolean and string observations. Scaling uses double-precision arithmetic; conversion to MIDI integers uses nearest rounding with ties to even. Input endpoints reach the configured integer endpoints exactly. Only identical quantized values are suppressed, and only after the host confirms a successful send.

items.title: Python host boundary
items.text:
from fractions import Fraction
from meedee import codecs, messages
from envelfo.midi import CCTarget, Mapper, Mapping

mapper = Mapper(
    mappings=[Mapping(
        output="expression",
        target=CCTarget(channel=1, controller=11),
        input_minimum=0.0,
        input_maximum=1.0,
    )],
    byte_rate=1000,
    burst_bytes=64,
)

# values may be result.values from advance_patch(), or from an existing bridge.
# at is host-supplied monotonic admission time in exact Fraction seconds.
batch = mapper.prepare(at=Fraction(1, 4), values={"expression": 0.5})
completed = False
try:
    for message in batch.messages:
        if isinstance(message, messages.ControlChange):
            connection.send(codecs.encode(message))  # caller-owned meedee connection
        else:
            connection.send_command(message)
    mapper.confirm(batch)
    completed = True
finally:
    if not completed:
        mapper.report_loss()

Serialize all calls to one mapper, and dedicate it to one output connection. Pass the original batch to confirm. A batch with no changed messages still requires confirmation, advancing the accepted admission time without byte cost. Do not alter the batch's list of messages. Confirmation rejects an altered list, a copied/foreign batch, or a stale batch. It does not prove instrument receipt: a successful backend send means acceptance under meedee's transport contract.

Rust uses the same flow with Mapper::prepare(at: Time, values: &BTreeMap<...>) and Mapper::confirm(&batch). batch.messages() contains MidiMessage variants wrapping meedee's immutable primitive/command values. Match those variants to OutputConnection::send or send_command; keep each compound command intact. MidiMessage::expand() exposes primitive order for device-free realization or inspection. Time uses enveLFO's existing checked signed-64-bit rational type; arithmetic overflow is an explicit error. Python uses exact Fraction seconds. See the crate documentation for a compiled public API example.

items.title: Admission and recovery
items.text:
Both rate and burst capacity are required. The token bucket starts full and refills in the supplied host admission clock. Admission time must not decrease. The complete first batch must fit the configured burst. Accounting includes each status byte and every expanded selector, data and RPN-null message; it does not assume running-status compression. For example, a fine CC costs six bytes, a 7-bit parameter Set costs fifteen and a 14-bit Set costs eighteen.

The limit covers this mapper's admitted MIDI bytes, not unrelated traffic, transport framing, driver buffers or a guaranteed hardware link rate. It is not a scheduler: it does not sleep, select observation cadence, estimate backend drain time or compensate for a host delivering an old batch late. Hosts must supply admission times matching their actual send scheduling. Transport sends can still block or fail after admission; select isolation and native deadlines at the host.

An over-budget observation is rejected before returning a batch, with no retained or coalesced update. No old values are silently flushed later. Invalid input, backward time and budget rejection leave mapper state unchanged. There is one pending batch at most; another prepare is refused until that batch is confirmed or the session is explicitly abandoned. Storage is proportional to configured mappings plus that batch, not elapsed time or observation count. Caller-held results and backend buffers are outside this bound. This is not an allocation- free real-time audio callback interface.

On a partial or uncertain send, interruption, reconnect or known output loss, call report_loss(). It invalidates suppression and abandons pending work without sending cleanup or retrying. A compound-send error's known prefix belongs to the host; the mapper never assumes the remaining bytes were delivered. There is no rollback of a command that already affected an instrument.

Only after the host has recovered its output session should it call restart(). The new session begins with a full budget and no suppression history; its first observation sends every configured target. Old batches cannot confirm new work. Restart sends no MIDI. Neither mapper runtime has a serialized continuation contract. Save application/transport state explicitly if continuation is needed.

items.title: Existing arpeg composition
items.text:
Keep the existing arpeg.envelfo.EnveLFOBridge and Rust arpeg-envelfo bridge. Their observations already expose named floating-point values in the shape this mapper accepts. The mapper does not receive hits or re-observe the Patch.

Preserve the existing schedule, receive same-time hits, observe once, then realize sequence described in arpeg's bridge contract. The player's owned breath, bend and pressure lanes continue through its existing realization path. Do not map those lanes a second time onto the same destination. For additional named controls, the host merges the prepared messages into its existing ordered delivery, keeping due releases and entry controls before fresh NoteOn. Sending these controls after the note is not equivalent for instruments that latch state at onset. This slice supplies the mapper; it does not modify arpeg's host or introduce another scheduling/bridge path.

items.title: Verification
items.text:
Python and Rust consume the same hand-authored wire and lifecycle cases, covering target families, ordering, integer endpoints, ties to even, confirmed suppression, exact refill, rejected work and explicit loss/restart. Additional unit checks cover foreign/stale batches, malformed configuration and non-finite values.

uv run --frozen --extra midi pytest
CARGO_HOME="$PWD/target/cargo-home" cargo test -p envelfo-midi --locked
CARGO_HOME="$PWD/target/cargo-home" cargo test -p envelfo-midi --locked --release

For authorized macOS qualification, invoke this as a standalone command:

uv run --frozen --extra midi pytest -q -s -n 0 test/qualification/midi_output.py

Each case has a 45-second outer deadline. Both isolated and in-process cases passed locally: exact ordered CC/fine-CC/RPN/NRPN delivery, confirmed suppression and explicit send failure after caller-owned close. Endpoints are uniquely named and test-owned. No physical devices, audio playback, tuning or reset messages are used. Linux/Windows native delivery and physical-device qualification remain open. Release CI adds device-free MIDI checks on Linux, Windows and macOS, without changing the release-only workflow trigger.

items.title: Rust performance and allocation audit
items.text: Measured on macOS arm64 with Homebrew Rust 1.99.0. These are local steady-state microbenchmarks, not portable latency promises or allocation-free callback claims.

items.title: Reproduction
items.text:
cargo bench -p envelfo-core --bench patch --locked

The dependency-free harness uses 256 warmup operations, then five timed runs of 4000 operations. It reports median/min/max of the five per-run averages in nanoseconds per operation, not individual-call tail latency. Allocations are counted in a separate run, including reallocations and requested bytes, not peak live memory. Preparation and warmup are excluded. Returned results and state clones are consumed with black_box and dropped inside the measured operation. The counting System allocator is confined to the benchmark executable; the library retains forbid(unsafe_code). The inactive counting check remains in the allocator during timed runs, equally for baseline and optimized measurements. Startup, snapshot JSON and host IO are not measured. macOS denied native sampler attachment, so this audit uses paired workload and clone-only measurements rather than claiming a sampled stack profile.

Patch workloads observe at 1024 Hz. The arpeg cases use two children and two outputs, with or without an explicit Envelope start before every observation. The signal case has 64 LFOs, 64 Slews and 64 outputs. The staged case has 16 independent marked LFO Stages. Fanout cases route a 64 Hz marker to 128 SampleHolds with 1/16-second delays and deterministic or 50% chance gates. Clone-only cases use separately warmed state, including queued deliveries, without advancing it.

Cloning is not the dominant CPU cost in these dense cases. The runtime also copies graph names into temporary signal maps and constructs connection stream identities before determining whether they are needed. Optimization starts there; transactional clones, exact rational times and event-capacity policies stay intact.

items.title: Optimized results
items.text:
The unchanged harness was rerun after optimization. This table records the final repeat's five-sample medians; an earlier run showed transient timing outliers, so these are reproducible local observations, not platform-independent guarantees. Allocation counts and requested bytes were stable between runs.

Workload Before ns/op After ns/op Before calls/op After calls/op After bytes/op Scalar LFO 292 288 0 0 0 arpeg observation 1220 1001 12 10 1177 arpeg start + observation 1764 1574 17 15 1630 Signals, 128 nodes 43857 36514 224 96 39443 Stages, 16 nodes 17588 14358 44.18 28.18 6366.65 Fanout, 128 connections 29425 19896 199.75 30.75 72892.81 Chance fanout, 128 connections 24873 15206 199.66 30.66 56074.75

Dense routing takes 32–39% less elapsed time and makes approximately 85% fewer allocation calls. The signal graph makes 57% fewer allocation calls and takes 17% less time. Small arpeg and staged workloads also improve; scalar LFO timing is unchanged within noise. Requested bytes fall less dramatically than allocation counts because transactional state/queue storage is retained.

Changes are limited to:

  • Borrow graph-owned names in the temporary signal map. The public owned-map Operator::observe API and the internal borrowed map use one evaluator.
  • Construct a connection's stream identity only when initializing its random stream. Gated-out, deterministic, pre-keyed and already-seeded routes avoid that string construction, without changing any stream key or draw.
  • Return unchanged position state when elapsed time is exactly zero. This skips redundant rational arithmetic in repeated staged observations, not nonzero advancement or overflow checks.

No public API, snapshot wire layout, capacity, event ordering, output ownership or default dependency changed. Advance/command/settle still clone and commit state only after success; no rollback journal or persistent scratch cache was added. This remains an allocating API, not a hard-real-time callback interface.

items.title: Correctness checks
items.text:
The Rust suites run with snapshots disabled and enabled, in debug and release, alongside formatting and strict Clippy checks. Shared body, host-clock, graph and random traces remain unchanged, including JSON continuation with pending events. Existing failure tests check state equality after arithmetic overflow, host-clock failures, event-order errors and both capacity limits. A new late-failure regression first executes chance routing and a random sample delivery, then fails on a missing host input or overflowing signal after a Slew update. The entire state must remain equal to its saved copy, and a corrected retry must match a clean run. A focused Stage regression also verifies that repeated observations at an already-consumed exact boundary do not replay events or mutate state, and that backwards time still errors without mutation.

Only the standalone core changed. Consumer dependency pins were not refreshed, and Linux/Windows testing remains a release gate rather than a per-commit action.

class Mapping(BaseModel, frozen=True):
    output: str = Field(min_length=1)
    target: CCTarget | FineCCTarget | RpnTarget | NrpnTarget = Field(
        discriminator='kind'
    )
    input_minimum: float
    input_maximum: float
    minimum: int = 0
    maximum: int | None = None

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def check_ranges(self) -> Self:
        if not (
            isfinite(self.input_minimum)
            and isfinite(self.input_maximum)
            and self.input_minimum < self.input_maximum
            and isfinite(self.input_maximum - self.input_minimum)
        ):
            raise ValueError('input bounds must define a finite increasing range')
        limit = _value_limit(self.target)
        maximum = limit if self.maximum is None else self.maximum
        if not 0 <= self.minimum <= maximum <= limit:
            raise ValueError('output bounds must lie within the target range')
        return self

    model_config = {'extra': 'forbid', 'strict': True}

items.title: Mapper
items.text:
One serialized caller per output connection, with explicit send completion.

prepare() reserves one batch; confirm() commits its values and byte budget. On any partial/uncertain send or known output loss, call report_loss().

Source code in envelfo/midi.py 
class Mapper:
    """One serialized caller per output connection, with explicit send completion.

    prepare() reserves one batch; confirm() commits its values and byte budget.
    On any partial/uncertain send or known output loss, call report_loss().
    """

    def __init__(
        self, *, mappings: list[Mapping], byte_rate: int, burst_bytes: int
    ) -> None:
        if not mappings:
            raise ValueError('at least one MIDI mapping is required')
        for value in [byte_rate, burst_bytes]:
            if type(value) is not int or not 0 < value <= 2**63 - 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    'byte rate and burst must be positive signed-64-bit integers'
                )
        destinations = [_destination(m.target) for m in mappings]
        if len(set(destinations)) != len(destinations):
            raise ValueError('MIDI destinations must be distinct')
        initial_bytes = sum(_wire_bytes(_message(m.target, 0)) for m in mappings)
        if initial_bytes > burst_bytes:
            raise ValueError('burst must accommodate the complete initial batch')
        self._mappings = mappings.copy()
        self._rate = byte_rate
        self._burst = burst_bytes
        self._tokens = Fraction(burst_bytes)
        self._at: Fraction | None = None
        self._values: list[int] | None = None
        self._pending: (
            tuple[Batch, list[messages.Message], list[int], Fraction] | None
        ) = None
        self._failed = False

    def prepare(self, *, at: Fraction, values: dict[str, float]) -> Batch:
        """Quantize a complete observation, without advancing a graph or sending."""
        if self._failed:
            raise RuntimeError('MIDI mapper requires explicit restart')
        if self._pending is not None:
            raise RuntimeError('confirm the pending batch before preparing another')
        if not isinstance(at, Fraction):
            raise TypeError('at must be exact Fraction host seconds')
        if self._at is not None and at < self._at:
            raise ValueError('MIDI observation time must not move backward')
        quantized: list[int] = []
        outgoing: list[
            messages.ControlChange
            | messages.ControlChange14
            | messages.RpnSet
            | messages.NrpnSet
        ] = []
        for i, mapping in enumerate(self._mappings):
            if mapping.output not in values:
                raise ValueError(f'missing mapped output: {mapping.output}')
            value = values[mapping.output]
            if type(value) not in (int, float) or not (
                mapping.input_minimum <= value <= mapping.input_maximum
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    f'output outside its finite input range: {mapping.output}'
                )
            maximum = (
                _value_limit(mapping.target)
                if mapping.maximum is None
                else mapping.maximum
            )
            normalized = (value - mapping.input_minimum) / (
                mapping.input_maximum - mapping.input_minimum
            )
            rounded = round(mapping.minimum + normalized * (maximum - mapping.minimum))
            quantized.append(rounded)
            if self._values is None or self._values[i] != rounded:
                outgoing.append(_message(mapping.target, rounded))
        size = sum(_wire_bytes(m) for m in outgoing)
        tokens = self._tokens
        if self._at is not None:
            tokens = min(Fraction(self._burst), tokens + (at - self._at) * self._rate)
        if size > tokens:
            raise OverflowError('MIDI wire-byte budget exhausted; no batch admitted')
        batch = Batch(at=at, messages=outgoing, wire_bytes=size)
        self._pending = batch, list(outgoing), quantized, tokens - size
        return batch

    def confirm(self, batch: Batch) -> None:
        """Confirm every message was sent successfully, not merely queued by a host."""
        if self._pending is None or batch is not self._pending[0]:
            raise ValueError("batch is not this mapper's pending batch")
        if batch.messages != self._pending[1]:
            raise ValueError('pending batch messages were altered')
        self._values = self._pending[2]
        self._tokens = self._pending[3]
        self._at = batch.at
        self._pending = None

    def report_loss(self) -> None:
        """Invalidate suppression and pending work; send no cleanup or retry."""
        self._pending = None
        self._values = None
        self._failed = True

    def restart(self) -> None:
        """Start an explicitly recovered output session with a fresh full budget."""
        self._pending = None
        self._values = None
        self._tokens = Fraction(self._burst)
        self._at = None
        self._failed = False

def prepare(self, *, at: Fraction, values: dict[str, float]) -> Batch:
    """Quantize a complete observation, without advancing a graph or sending."""
    if self._failed:
        raise RuntimeError('MIDI mapper requires explicit restart')
    if self._pending is not None:
        raise RuntimeError('confirm the pending batch before preparing another')
    if not isinstance(at, Fraction):
        raise TypeError('at must be exact Fraction host seconds')
    if self._at is not None and at < self._at:
        raise ValueError('MIDI observation time must not move backward')
    quantized: list[int] = []
    outgoing: list[
        messages.ControlChange
        | messages.ControlChange14
        | messages.RpnSet
        | messages.NrpnSet
    ] = []
    for i, mapping in enumerate(self._mappings):
        if mapping.output not in values:
            raise ValueError(f'missing mapped output: {mapping.output}')
        value = values[mapping.output]
        if type(value) not in (int, float) or not (
            mapping.input_minimum <= value <= mapping.input_maximum
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f'output outside its finite input range: {mapping.output}'
            )
        maximum = (
            _value_limit(mapping.target)
            if mapping.maximum is None
            else mapping.maximum
        )
        normalized = (value - mapping.input_minimum) / (
            mapping.input_maximum - mapping.input_minimum
        )
        rounded = round(mapping.minimum + normalized * (maximum - mapping.minimum))
        quantized.append(rounded)
        if self._values is None or self._values[i] != rounded:
            outgoing.append(_message(mapping.target, rounded))
    size = sum(_wire_bytes(m) for m in outgoing)
    tokens = self._tokens
    if self._at is not None:
        tokens = min(Fraction(self._burst), tokens + (at - self._at) * self._rate)
    if size > tokens:
        raise OverflowError('MIDI wire-byte budget exhausted; no batch admitted')
    batch = Batch(at=at, messages=outgoing, wire_bytes=size)
    self._pending = batch, list(outgoing), quantized, tokens - size
    return batch

class PreparedPatch(Model, frozen=True):
    """Materialized host graph; executable children retain their own clocks.

    Authored Patches still inherit clock/scope in uFor. This execution boundary
    also joins independently authored generators without changing their models.
    """

    envelfos: dict[
        str,
        envelfo.LFO
        | envelfo.Envelope
        | envelfo.Stages
        | envelfo.SampleHold
        | envelfo.Sum
        | envelfo.Product
        | envelfo.Affine
        | envelfo.Quantize
        | envelfo.Latch
        | envelfo.Threshold
        | envelfo.Slew,
    ]
    outputs: dict[str, str]
    events: list[envelfo.PatchEventConnection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    event_outputs: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    inputs: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    sample_keys: dict[str, int] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    connection_identities: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @cached_property
    def signal_order(self) -> list[str]:
        graph = {
            n: b.inputs
            if isinstance(b, (envelfo.Sum, envelfo.Product))
            else [b.input]
            if isinstance(
                b,
                (
                    envelfo.Affine,
                    envelfo.Quantize,
                    envelfo.Latch,
                    envelfo.Threshold,
                    envelfo.Slew,
                ),
            )
            else []
            for n, b in self.envelfos.items()
        }
        return list(TopologicalSorter(graph).static_order())

def connection_gate(
    count: int | None,
    random_state: int | None,
    every: int,
    offset: int,
    probability: float,
    seed: int,
    identity: str,
) -> tuple[int, int | None, bool]:
    """First-aligned division; draw only for eligible, nonconstant chance gates."""
    count = offset if count is None else count
    remaining = every - 1 if count == 0 else count - 1
    threshold = int(probability * 2**53)
    if count != 0 or threshold == 0:
        return remaining, random_state, False
    if threshold == 2**53:
        return remaining, random_state, True
    if random_state is None:
        random_state = seed ^ envelfo_random.stream_key(0, identity)
    random_state, word = random.random_word(random_state)
    return remaining, random_state, word >> 11 < threshold

def observe_signals(
    body: envelfo.Patch | PreparedPatch,
    signals: dict[str, float],
    retained: dict[str, float],
    seconds: Fraction,
) -> tuple[dict[str, float], dict[str, float], list[tuple[str, str]]]:
    """Evaluate one host observation; missing pruned inputs stay absent."""
    signals, retained = dict(signals), dict(retained)
    emitted: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for name in body.signal_order:
        child = body.envelfos[name]
        if isinstance(child, (envelfo.Sum, envelfo.Product)):
            if all(n in signals for n in child.inputs):
                signals[name] = runtime.transform_value(child, signals)
        elif isinstance(child, (envelfo.Affine, envelfo.Quantize)):
            if child.input in signals:
                signals[name] = runtime.transform_value(child, signals)
        elif isinstance(child, (envelfo.Latch, envelfo.Threshold, envelfo.Slew)):
            if child.input not in signals:
                continue
            value = signals[child.input]
            if isinstance(child, envelfo.Latch):
                value = runtime.latch_value(value, retained.get(name))
            elif isinstance(child, envelfo.Slew):
                value = runtime.slew_value(child, value, retained.get(name), seconds)
            else:
                value, port = runtime.threshold_value(child, value, retained.get(name))
                if port is not None:
                    emitted.append((name, port))
            retained[name] = signals[name] = value
    return signals, retained, emitted

def initial_patch(
    definition: envelfo.EnveLFO | PreparedPatch,
    at: Fraction,
    *,
    name: str = 'patch',
    seed: int = 0,
    tempo_map: control.TempoMap | None = None,
) -> PatchState:
    """Initialize child state without inventing note-on events or observations."""
    body = _body(definition)
    children = {
        n: runtime.initial_envelfo(
            _child(definition, n),
            _clock(definition, at, tempo_map, n),
            seed=seed
            ^ (
                definition.sample_keys.get(
                    n, envelfo_random.stream_key(0, f'patch-{name}-{n}:sample-hold')
                )
                if isinstance(definition, PreparedPatch)
                else envelfo_random.stream_key(0, f'patch-{name}-{n}:sample-hold')
            )
            if isinstance(b, envelfo.SampleHold)
            else 0,
        )
        for n, b in body.envelfos.items()
        if isinstance(
            b, (envelfo.LFO, envelfo.Envelope, envelfo.Stages, envelfo.SampleHold)
        )
        and not (isinstance(definition, PreparedPatch) and n in definition.inputs)
    }
    return PatchState(at=at, cursor=at, name=name, seed=seed, children=children)

def advance_patch(
    definition: envelfo.EnveLFO | PreparedPatch,
    state: PatchState,
    at: Fraction,
    *,
    next_delivery: Fraction,
    tempo_map: control.TempoMap | None = None,
    inputs: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> PatchAdvance:
    """Process boundaries/deliveries, then observe once on the host's schedule."""
    if next_delivery <= at:
        raise ValueError('next delivery must follow the observation')
    control.elapsed(at, state.at)
    state = _copy_state(state)
    if inputs is not None:
        state = state.model_copy(update={'inputs': dict(inputs)})
    state, emitted = _run(definition, state, at, tempo_map, True)
    state = state.model_copy(update={'at': at})
    signals = dict(state.inputs)
    for name, child_state in state.children.items():
        value = runtime.envelfo_at(
            _child(definition, name),
            child_state,
            _clock(definition, at, tempo_map, name),
        )
        signals[name] = value.value * value.weight
    values, retained, edges = observe_signals(
        _body(definition),
        signals,
        state.retained,
        Fraction(0) if state.observed_at is None else at - state.observed_at,
    )
    state = state.model_copy(update={'retained': retained, 'observed_at': at})
    for name, port in edges:
        emitted.extend(
            _route(
                definition,
                state,
                name,
                envelfo.EnvelfoOutputEvent(
                    at=next_delivery,
                    port=port,
                    stage=name,
                    activation=0,
                ),
                next_delivery,
            )
        )
    return PatchAdvance(
        state=state,
        values={n: values[c] for n, c in _body(definition).outputs.items()},
        events=emitted,
    )

def patch_event(
    definition: envelfo.EnveLFO | PreparedPatch,
    state: PatchState,
    target: str,
    event: envelfo.EnvelfoEvent,
    *,
    tempo_map: control.TempoMap | None = None,
    inclusive: bool = True,
) -> tuple[PatchState, list[envelfo.EnvelfoOutputEvent]]:
    """Deliver a child command in host seconds, without observing the graph."""
    control.elapsed(event.at, state.at)
    state = _copy_state(state)
    state, emitted = _run(definition, state, event.at, tempo_map, False)
    emitted.extend(_command(definition, state, target, event, tempo_map))
    if inclusive:
        state, output = _run(definition, state, event.at, tempo_map, True)
        emitted.extend(output)
    return state.model_copy(update={'at': event.at}), emitted

Source code in envelfo/patch.py 
def observe_block(
    definition: PreparedPatch, signals: dict[str, list[float]]
) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
    """Observe stateless operators over host-sampled event-free leaf spans."""
    if any(
        isinstance(b, (envelfo.Latch, envelfo.Threshold, envelfo.Slew))
        for b in definition.envelfos.values()
    ):
        raise ValueError('retained Patch operators require individual observations')
    if not signals:
        return {}
    output = {n: [] for n in definition.outputs}
    for i in range(len(next(iter(signals.values())))):
        values, _, _ = observe_signals(
            definition, {n: v[i] for n, v in signals.items()}, {}, Fraction(0)
        )
        for name, child in definition.outputs.items():
            output[name].append(values[child])
    return output

def random_word(state: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    state = (state + 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15) & 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
    word = ((state ^ (state >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9) & 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
    word = ((word ^ (word >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB) & 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
    return state, word ^ (word >> 31)

Source code in envelfo/runtime.py 
def slew_value(
    body: envelfo.Slew, value: float, previous: float | None, seconds: Fraction
) -> float:
    """Limit one observation in signal units per second, without overshoot."""
    if previous is None:
        return value if body.initial is None else body.initial
    elapsed = float(seconds)
    if value >= previous:
        return min(value, previous + body.rise * elapsed)
    return max(value, previous - body.fall * elapsed)

def threshold_value(
    body: envelfo.Threshold, value: float, previous: float | None
) -> tuple[float, str | None]:
    """Observe one grid sample; initialization is silent and deadband holds state."""
    output = float(value >= body.upper) if previous is None else previous
    if previous == 0 and value >= body.upper:
        return 1.0, 'rising'
    if previous == 1 and value <= body.lower:
        return 0.0, 'falling'
    return output, None

def envelope_complete_at(
    definition: envelfo.Envelope, state: envelfo.EnvelfoState
) -> Fraction | None:
    """Release completion in the owning clock, or None while completion is unbounded."""
    runtime = state.runtime
    if not isinstance(runtime, envelfo.EnvelopeState):
        raise ValueError('Envelope completion requires Envelope state')
    if runtime.phase != 'release':
        return None
    parts = definition.release[runtime.segment_index :]
    if any(s.duration is None for s in parts):
        return None
    total = sum(
        (s.duration for s in parts if isinstance(s, segments.Segment)), Fraction(0)
    )
    position = runtime.position
    target = total if _indefinite(definition) else Fraction(1)
    if not total or position.coordinate >= target:
        return position.at
    if position.paused or position.direction == -1 or not position.rate:
        return None
    return position.at + (target - position.coordinate) / position.rate

def advance_envelfo(
    definition: envelfo.EnveLFO,
    state: envelfo.EnvelfoState,
    at: Fraction,
    event: envelfo.EnvelfoEvent | None = None,
) -> envelfo.EnvelfoAdvance:
    """Advance a staged Envelfo, returning its state and ordered output events."""
    body = definition
    runtime = state.runtime
    if not isinstance(body, envelfo.Stages) or not isinstance(
        runtime, envelfo.StageState
    ):
        raise ValueError('advance_envelfo requires staged Envelfo state')
    control.elapsed(at, runtime.at)
    if event is not None:
        if event.at != at:
            raise ValueError('Envelfo event time must equal the advance boundary')
        control.check_order(runtime.at, runtime.ordinal, event)
    current, emitted = _advance_stages(body, runtime, at, event is None)
    if event is not None:
        if event.action in ('pause', 'resume', 'reverse', 'seek', 'shift', 'rate'):
            stage = next(s.envelfo for s in body.stages if s.name == current.stage)
            if (
                event.action in ('seek', 'shift')
                and isinstance(stage, envelfo.Envelope)
                and _indefinite(stage)
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    'indefinite envelopes do not accept normalized position events'
                )
            position = _position_command(_position_at(current.position, at), event)
            if (
                event.action == 'shift'
                and isinstance(stage, envelfo.Envelope)
                and stage.playback == envelfo.PlaybackMode.once
            ):
                position = position.model_copy(
                    update={
                        'coordinate': max(
                            Fraction(0), min(Fraction(1), position.coordinate)
                        )
                    }
                )
            current = current.model_copy(
                update={
                    'position': position,
                    'cursor_order': -1,
                }
            )
        elif event.action == 'advance':
            stage = next(s.envelfo for s in body.stages if s.name == current.stage)
            if not isinstance(stage, envelfo.Envelope) or current.completed:
                raise ValueError('advance requires an active indefinite segment')
            position = _position_at(current.position, at)
            index, value = _advance_segment(
                stage.segments,
                current.segment_index,
                current.entry_value,
                position.coordinate,
                _indefinite(stage),
            )
            current = current.model_copy(
                update={
                    'at': at,
                    'segment_index': index,
                    'entry_value': value,
                    'stage_done': False,
                    'position': position.model_copy(update={'coordinate': Fraction(0)}),
                    'cursor_order': -1,
                }
            )
            current, output = _advance_stages(body, current, at, True)
            emitted.extend(output)
        else:
            key = f'cue.{event.cue}' if event.action == 'cue' else event.action
            activation = current.activation
            current, output = _stage_transition(body, current, at, key)
            emitted.extend(output)
            if current.activation == activation and not current.completed:
                current, output = _advance_stages(body, current, at, True)
                emitted.extend(output)
        current = current.model_copy(
            update={
                'at': at,
                'ordinal': event.ordinal,
                'cursor_order': current.cursor_order,
            }
        )
    value = _stage_value(body, current, at)
    return envelfo.EnvelfoAdvance(
        state=envelfo.EnvelfoState(runtime=current), value=value, events=emitted
    )

def next_stage_event(
    body: envelfo.Stages,
    state: envelfo.StageState,
    limit: Fraction,
    inclusive: bool = True,
) -> tuple[Fraction, int, str] | None:
    """Find the next natural boundary without advancing state or emitting events."""
    if state.completed:
        return None
    stage = next(s.envelfo for s in body.stages if s.name == state.stage)
    if (
        isinstance(stage, envelfo.Envelope)
        and _indefinite(stage)
        and not state.stage_done
        and all(s.duration == 0 for s in stage.segments[state.segment_index :])
    ):
        return (
            (state.at, 0, 'done')
            if (state.at <= limit if inclusive else state.at < limit)
            else None
        )
    candidates: list[tuple[Fraction, int, str]] = []
    position = state.position
    if position.paused or not position.rate:
        return None
    start = position.coordinate
    forward = position.direction == 1
    if isinstance(stage, envelfo.Envelope):
        if _indefinite(stage):
            remaining = stage.segments[state.segment_index :]
            if any(s.duration is None for s in remaining):
                return None
            target = sum(
                (s.duration for s in remaining if isinstance(s, segments.Segment)),
                Fraction(0),
            )
            if forward and (start < target or start == target and not state.stage_done):
                candidates.append(
                    (state.at + (target - start) / position.rate, 0, 'done')
                )
        elif stage.playback == envelfo.PlaybackMode.once:
            for index, marker in enumerate(stage.markers):
                target = marker.position
                if (target > start if forward else target < start) or (
                    target == start
                    and state.cursor_order >= 0
                    and (
                        index > state.cursor_order
                        if forward
                        else index < state.cursor_order
                    )
                ):
                    time = state.at + abs(target - start) / position.rate
                    candidates.append((time, index, marker.name))
            if forward and (
                start < 1
                or (start == 1 and 0 <= state.cursor_order < len(stage.markers))
            ):
                candidates.append(
                    (state.at + (1 - start) / position.rate, len(stage.markers), 'done')
                )
        elif stage.loop_start is not None:
            candidates.extend(_named_loop_candidates(stage, state))
        else:
            period = 1 if stage.playback == envelfo.PlaybackMode.loop else 2
            for index, marker in enumerate(stage.markers):
                offsets = (
                    [marker.position]
                    if period == 1
                    else [marker.position, 2 - marker.position]
                )
                for offset in offsets:
                    turn = (
                        floor((start - offset) / period) + 1
                        if forward
                        else ceil((start - offset) / period) - 1
                    )
                    target = turn * period + offset
                    candidates.append(
                        (
                            state.at + abs(target - start) / position.rate,
                            index,
                            marker.name,
                        )
                    )
                    if (
                        state.cursor_order >= 0
                        and (start - offset) % period == 0
                        and (
                            index > state.cursor_order
                            if forward
                            else index < state.cursor_order
                        )
                    ):
                        candidates.append((state.at, index, marker.name))
            boundary = floor(start) + 1 if forward else ceil(start) - 1
            order = len(stage.markers)
            candidates.append(
                (
                    state.at + abs(boundary - start) / position.rate,
                    order,
                    'cycle' if period == 1 else 'turned',
                )
            )
            if period == 2 and boundary % 2 == 0:
                candidates.append(
                    (
                        state.at + abs(boundary - start) / position.rate,
                        order + 1,
                        'cycle',
                    )
                )
            if period == 2 and start.denominator == 1 and start % 2 == 0:
                if state.cursor_order == order:
                    candidates.append((state.at, order + 1, 'cycle'))
    else:
        assert isinstance(stage, envelfo.LFO)
        for index, marker in enumerate(stage.markers):
            offset = start - marker.position
            turn = floor(offset) + 1 if forward else ceil(offset) - 1
            target = turn + marker.position
            time = state.at + abs(target - start) / position.rate
            candidates.append((time, index, marker.name))
            if (
                state.cursor_order >= 0
                and offset.denominator == 1
                and (
                    index > state.cursor_order
                    if forward
                    else index < state.cursor_order
                )
            ):
                candidates.append((state.at, index, marker.name))
    available = [
        c for c in candidates if (c[0] <= limit if inclusive else c[0] < limit)
    ]
    if not available:
        return None
    return (
        min(available)
        if forward
        else min(
            available,
            key=lambda c: (
                c[0],
                c[1] if c[2] in ('turned', 'cycle') else -c[1],
            ),
        )
    )
